proven_findings: MajorMUD uses retained Worldgroup DFA context rather than passing a complete transaction object to every operation.
Mutation operations are distinct imported calls: insert, update, and delete are not implicit side effects of reset.
The dominant lock-acquisition shape has five stack positions and a lock-mode constant in position four.
Observed lock-mode constants include 5, 8, 9, 10, 12, and 13; semantic names remain unresolved except mode 9 already proven on textblock fetch.
Reset/release is explicit through _dfaRstBlk and absolute-position cleanup through _dfaAbs.

No separate MajorMUD-imported commit, rollback, journal, or checksum symbol is present in the recovered DFA import family; those semantics, if any, are internal to Worldgroup or a lower storage module.
limits: This pass does not claim the internal on-disk commit algorithm.
Lock-mode names are not invented from numeric constants.
Crash recovery, journaling, backup rotation, and checksum behavior remain unresolved.
